papers.title: Last-Iterate Convergence of Payoff-Gradient Learning in M\"obius Pricing Games
papers.abstract: We prove global last-iterate convergence of payoff-gradient learning in every typewise Riemannian metric, which for scalar actions is the same as typewise mirror descent, with explicit rates, in a class of Bayesian bidding and pricing games that includes first-price auctions, unit-demand pay-as-bid auctions, rank-based generalized first-price auctions, and homogeneous-good price competition with inelastic demand. The result holds for symmetric self-play: all players use a common strategy and apply the same payoff-gradient update at each type. Convergence is from every continuous weakly increasing feasible initial strategy, including pooling, and does not rely on the monotonicity or Minty conditions that underlie existing guarantees in other games. Instead, the class is characterized by two structural properties: a direct payoff effect that is independent of the action, and a payoff difference at the allocation threshold that is affine in the action. These properties reduce the learning dynamics to a singular transport-damping equation for the common strategy, which, under the stated coefficient and metric assumptions, admits a unique viscosity solution. Comparison barriers make the uniform distance to the unique rest point a strict Lyapunov functional and yield convergence rates with optimal algebraic exponents. In allocation games, the rest point is the unique weakly increasing symmetric equilibrium under the stated tie-breaking conditions, and a positive lower slope bound converts strategy-error bounds into explicit approximate-equilibrium guarantees. A projected grid scheme with a slope floor makes the approximation constructive, with error bounds under deterministic perturbations and almost-sure convergence on a fixed grid under martingale gradient noise.

papers.title: Quantitative Convergence of Hit-and-Run Beyond Log-Concavity via Variational Hypocoercivity
papers.abstract: We study the convergence to equilibrium of Hit-and-Run, a popular generalisation of the Gibbs sampler. To this end, we establish a novel connection between Hit-and-Run and the theory of variational hypocoercivity, an approach to establish convergence of continuous-time Markov processes. To bridge the gap between the discrete-time Hit-and-Run chain and hypocoercivity, we introduce Hit-and-Langevin, a continuous-time Markov process that approximates Hit-and-Run in an appropriate sense. Using the second-order lift and flow Poincar\'e inequality formulation of variational hypocoercivity, we show convergence of Hit-and-Langevin and deduce a lower bound on the spectral gap of Hit-and-Run. Notably, our analysis seamlessly extends beyond the extensively studied setting of log-concave target distributions, marking the first substantial departure from this setting beyond quasi-log-concave and uniform distributions. More broadly, this work demonstrates that discrete, non-local dynamics, such as Hit-and-Run, can be made amenable to powerful analytical methods, such as variational hypocoercivity.

papers.title: Ordering error estimates under mesh-uniform regularity and optimal two-mesh design for the KdV equation with boundary dissipation
papers.abstract: We study Galerkin error estimates and optimal two-mesh design for the Korteweg-de Vries (KdV) equation on a bounded interval with boundary dissipation. The ordering error is introduced to measure how much the nonlinearity changes the discretization error. A weighted cubic Hermite Galerkin scheme has mesh-uniform regularity: the discrete semigroups of the linearized equation inherit Crandall-Pazy regularity and Kato smoothing, with bounds uniform in the mesh size $h$. On a small ball of the energy space, the discrete solution maps are also analytic in the initial datum, with bounds uniform in $h$. On this ball the ordering error is at most of order $h^{1/6}$ times the squared energy norm of the datum, for all $t\ge0$. For $u_0$ on this ball and in the domain $D(A)$ of the linearized generator, the bound is of order $h^2\|u_0\|_{H^3}^{3/2}\|u_0\|_{L^2}^{1/2}$. A two-mesh computation adds a nonlinear correction on a coarse mesh to a linear simulation on a fine mesh. Its error is the linear error on the fine mesh plus the ordering error on the coarse mesh. Based on these error estimates, we formulate a model of the optimal two-mesh design: minimize the cost subject to an accuracy constraint given by the error bounds. For data in a small ball of $L^2$, the problem is convex in logarithmic mesh sizes. When the relative error bound for the coarsest allowed mesh exceeds the prescribed tolerance $\eta$, the optimal pair and its KKT multipliers are unique. For smooth data the problem is convex in the mesh sizes, and the optimal mesh ratio is independent of the tolerance until the coarse mesh reaches its upper limit. In both cases we characterize the small-amplitude limit of the relative cost when the relative tolerance is proportional to the amplitude.

papers.title: A particle method for the space homogeneous Lenard-Balescu equation
papers.abstract: We propose a structure preserving particle method to numerically approximate the spatially homogeneous Lenard-Balescu equation for collisional plasmas. The Lenard-Balescu operator is an improvement of the Landau equation with a dielectric function taking the dynamic screening effect into account. Our particle method is based on the variational formulation of the Lenard-Balescu equation under suitable regularization analogous to the strategy followed for the Landau collision operator in [12]. The method guarantees the conservation laws and the entropy dissipation at the semi-discrete level. The novel difficulty of the nonlocal nonlinear dependence of the dielectric function is tackled by rewriting it as integrals in terms of orthogonal and parallel components to the frequency variable. This equivalent form reduces the evaluation of the dielectric function to numerically computing an integral of the directional derivative of the solution on a hyperplane orthogonal to the frequency variable and its one-dimensional Hilbert transform. An efficient implementation of the numerical approximation for the Lenard-Balescu kernel is derived by exploiting this expression of the dielectric function. We finally validate our method by means of several numerical tests, further allowing us to explore qualitative properties of the Lenard-Balescu equation.

papers.title: Convergence analysis of resonant frequency approximation in periodic Helmholtz problems
papers.abstract: We investigate resonant frequencies of the Helmholtz equation in periodic structures under quasi-periodic conditions, using approximations of the associated quasi-periodic Green function, which is represented by a lattice sum. By formulating the periodic Helmholtz problem using layer potential operators whose kernel is given by the quasi-periodic Green function, resonant frequencies correspond to characteristic values of an associated operator-valued function. Based on two approximation methods for the quasi-periodic Green function, the Ewald method and the shifted Green function method, we propose the corresponding approximation schemes for resonant frequencies. Furthermore, we establish convergence rates for the resulting approximations using Gohberg--Sigal theory, where the Ewald method yields exponential convergence, while the shifted Green function method yields algebraic convergence. Numerical computations are presented to validate and compare the proposed approximation schemes.

papers.title: The Stability of the Backward Problem for Photoacoustic Imaging in Attenuating Media via Carleman Estimates
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the backward problem in time for photoacoustic tomography (PAT) in attenuating media. It is well-established that photoacoustic imaging in attenuating media can be accurately modeled by spatial fractional-order damping. This inverse problem is ill-posed in the sense of Hadamard. In this work, we construct a novel class of Carleman estimates independent of spatial variables, and by virtue of these estimates, we establish conditional stability estimates for this problem for the first time. Building upon this, we propose a Tikhonov-type regularization functional and derive its associated adjoint system. Furthermore, leveraging the established conditional stability results, we derive the convergence rate of the proposed regularization approach. Finally, we validate the effectiveness of our theoretical findings through extensive numerical experiments.

papers.title: Corrigendum to "Well-posedness and regularity of the integral invariant model from linear scalar transport equation" [J. Math. Anal. Appl. 564 (2026) 130904]
papers.abstract: We clarify the compactly supported terminal test space and the moving-domain Bochner spaces in the integral invariant formulation. We complete the existence proof by establishing strong measurability and the initial trace, and replace the stability argument by a compact-test density argument that retains the original stability constant. A short appendix shows that the integral invariant identity remains valid for all square-integrable terminal test functions that vanish almost everywhere outside the terminal domain, thereby admitting the zero extensions of the cell polynomials used in the SLDG/SLFV method. We also correct the velocity and divergence in the swirling-deformation example.

papers.title: Generalized Caffarelli--Kohn--Nirenberg and related inequalities for Grushin-type gradients
papers.abstract:
In this paper, we establish necessary and sufficient conditions for a generalized Caffarelli--Kohn--Nirenberg inequality involving the Grushin-type gradient $
abla_G=(
abla_x,|x|^\alpha
abla_y)$, where $\alpha\geq0$, in arbitrary dimensions. When $\alpha=0$, our results recover the classical Caffarelli--Kohn--Nirenberg inequalities and extend the mixed radial and cylindrical weight inequalities of Li and Yan \cite{LY23} to arbitrary dimensions of the $y$ variables. Our approach combines a change of variables with approximation arguments to reduce the Grushin inequalities to Euclidean inequalities with mixed weights. We also characterize the admissible parameters in Hardy--Sobolev inequalities, including the endpoint cases $p=1$ and $q=p$, and derive multiplicative Sobolev and Gagliardo--Nirenberg inequalities. Finally, we establish a weighted Moser--Trudinger inequality on bounded domains and deduce exponential integrability for subcritical growth with arbitrary locally integrable cylindrical power weights. By letting $\alpha=0$, our results also yield the corresponding inequalities for the Euclidean gradient.

papers.title: On the mode stability of a self-similar blow-up of Yang--Mills heat flow in five dimensions
papers.abstract: We study the spectral stability properties of an explicitly known self-similar blowup profile to the Yang-Mills heat flow on $\mathbb R^5\times SO(5)$ often referred to as the Weinkove solution. We prove that this solution is mode stable in a dynamically evolving DeTurck gauge. To arrive at that result, we first reduce the problem to countably many vector-valued Schr\"odinger operators on the half line. We then proceed by proving uniform estimates for all but finitely many of said operators. The spectra of the remaining operators are studied individually by means of GGMT bounds or by comparison arguments. Two of these operators are distinguished as they have negative eigenvalues originating from symmetries. Among these two there is a scalar operator, previously analyzed by Donninger and Sch\"orkhuber, and an operator acting on a three-dimensional vector bundle. The latter operator's matrix structure prohibits a straightforward supersymmetric removal. To circumvent this, we transform the equation to a Schr\"odinger operator with drift terms to simplify the structure of the eigenfunction. We then develop tools to study such operators and conclude that said operator has no second negative eigenvalue.

papers.title: Nehari type characterizations of the mountain pass level on cones
papers.abstract: We relate the mountain pass level of a functional to its infimum over the part of the Nehari set formed by local maximizers of the fiber maps. {Unlike in the classical setting where every fiber map has a unique global maximizer,} the fiber maps need not all have a maximizer: working on each path-connected component of the cone of directions where they do, we show that the two levels coincide, for merely continuous functionals and without any compactness assumption. We also introduce a notion of mountain pass geometry with respect to a cone, which may hold when the classical one fails. {This geometry includes the zero-level case when a suitable separating set exists.} Under the Palais--Smale condition, each component carries a critical point at its own mountain pass level. Applications include indefinite and concave-convex problems with sign-changing weights, the affine $p$-Laplacian, nonlocal problems, and a problem related to the Fu\v{c}\'{\i}k spectrum.

papers.title: On the Planar Optimal Transport Problem
papers.abstract: We develop a complex analytic framework based on rotation of gradient graphs for the study of quadratic cost planar optimal transport with uniform densities. Using this framework we carry out the construction, characterization, and approximation of non-degenerate optimal transport maps up to the boundary. We also identify obstructions for continuous optimal transport and construct discontinuous optimal transport maps with prescribed analytic singular sets.

papers.title: Asymptotic analysis and uniqueness of positive solutions to slightly subcritical fractional problems in symmetric domains
papers.abstract: We prove that the fractional Lane-Emden problem \[ (-\Delta)^s u = u^{p}\quad \text{ in }\Omega, \qquad u>0\quad \text{ in }\Omega, \qquad u=0 \text{ in }\mathbb R^N\setminus\Omega, \] admits a unique and nondegenerate solution when $\Omega$ is a smooth and bounded domain which is symmetric and convex with respect to $N$ orthogonal directions and the exponent $p$ is slightly subcritical. This result is new even in the case when $\Omega$ is a ball and $N\geq 2$. Our proof relies on a sharp characterization of the asymptotic behavior of low energy solutions, which we develop in general smooth bounded open sets.

papers.title: Global well-posedness and scattering for the fractional inhomogeneous nonlinear Schrodinger equation with time-dependent damping
papers.abstract: In this paper, we prove the global well-posedness and scattering of solutions for a nonlinear Schrodinger type equation with fractional Laplacian, inhomogeneous nonlinearity and time-dependent damping.We give an elementary proof based on Strichartz estimates combined with estimates of the nonlinear term in mixed-norm spaces. To avoid the loss of regularity in the Strichartz estimates, we consider the radial data.

papers.title: Regularization for the inhomogeneous nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation in one dimension
papers.abstract: In this work, we investigate the initial data problem for the following inhomogeneous nonlinear Schr\"odinger (INLS) equation $$ i \partial_t u + \partial_x^2 u = \pm |x|^{-b} |u|^{2k} u, \quad u(0, x)= u_0(x),$$ where $b>0$ and $k\in \mathbb{Z}_{>0}$. The singular potential $|x|^{-b}$ impairs the Sobolev regularity that can be propagated by the flow. We establish the regularization mechanism of this model and prove local well-posedness in $H_x^{\alpha}$ for $\alpha=5/2-b-$. Moreover, at the endpoint space $H_x^{5/2-b}$, we show that there is no $C^{2k+1}$ flow map at the origin. The proof combines the one-dimensional local smoothing effect with a normal-form reduction for the high-low interaction generated by the singular part of the coefficient. The argument applies to both the focusing and defocusing cases.

papers.title: Finsler--Sobolev inequalities: optimality & rigidity
papers.abstract: We establish optimal Sobolev and logarithmic-Sobolev inequalities on non-compact, possibly non-reversible Finsler manifolds with non-negative weighted Ricci curvature. The optimal constants exhibit no dependence on reversibility -- confirming Ohta's conjectural principle -- being governed solely by the forward and backward asymptotic volume ratios. We then apply the logarithmic-Sobolev inequality to establish the optimal hypercontractivity estimate for the heat flow in the same geometric setting. The equality cases of the above optimal inequalities imply strong rigidity in the underlying manifold, characterized by fine properties of the flag and $S$-curvatures as well as the precise profiles of the corresponding extremizers. We illustrate our results by examples including Randers metrics obtained by Zermelo navigation with Killing vector fields, and weighted convex cones in $\mathbb{R}^n$ endowed with arbitrary Minkowski norms, the latter showing that the forward and backward asymptotic volume ratios may differ.

papers.title: Global existence and decay estimates for classical solutions to 2D compressible micropolar fluid equations with vacuum
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider the Cauchy problem for the two-dimensional compressible micropolar fluid equations with far field vacuum. Under the assumption that the initial energy is sufficiently small, we establish the global existence and uniqueness of strong and classical solutions, allowing for large oscillations in the initial data. The key to the proof is to derive {\it a priori} decay estimates for the pressure, the velocity gradient, and the microrotational velocity, which enable us to close the bootstrap argument. We also handle the difficulties arising from the coupling between the velocity field and the microrotational velocity.

papers.title: Weak-type bow shocks
papers.abstract: An existence proof is given for bow shocks ahead of blunt convex wedges that are transonic and of weak type at infinity, including cases for arbitrarily small shock strength. It is also proven that any such flow is necessarily univalent, meaning the position-to-velocity map is injective.

papers.title: Nonlinear Stability of Two-Dimensional Poiseuille Flow via a Dilation Multiplier
papers.abstract: We investigate nonlinear stability of the Poiseuille flow for 2D incompressible Navier Stokes equations.The key observation is that, after Fourier transformation, the Poiseuille flow and its curvature give rise to a kinetic operator and a potential whose commutators with the same bounded dilation multiplier are both nonnegative.To close the nonlinear estimates, we incorporate the zero mode of the initial velocity into the background shear flow, thereby further improving the threshold.

papers.title: Improved Singular Adams-type inequalities and the existence of extremals in dimension four
papers.abstract: Let $H_0^2(\Omega)$ denote the Sobolev space on $\Omega$, where $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^4$ is a smooth bounded domain containing the origin, and let $\lambda(\Omega)$ denote the first eigenvalue of the bi-Laplacian $\Delta^2$ on $\Omega$ subject to homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions. We establish the following singular Adams inequality of Adimurthi-Druet type: for $0<\beta<4$ and $0\leq\alpha<\lambda(\Omega)$, \[ \sup\limits_{{u\in H_0^2(\Omega),\|\Delta u\|_2^2=1}}\int_\Omega \frac{e^{32\pi^2(1-\frac{\beta}{4}) u^2(1+\alpha\|u\|_2^2)}}{|x|^\beta}dx < +\infty. \] Moreover, this supremum is infinite for $\alpha>\lambda_1(\Omega)$. Furthermore, we show the existence of extremal functions, that is, for sufficiently small $\alpha>0$, there exists $u^*\in H_0^2(\Omega)\cap C_{\mathrm{loc}}^4(\Omega\setminus{0})$ with $\|\Delta u^*\|_2^2=1$ such that \[ \int_\Omega \frac{e^{32\pi^2(1-\frac{\beta}{4}) {|u^*|}^2(1+\alpha\|u^*\|_2^2)}}{|x|^\beta}dx=\sup\limits_{{u\in H_0^2(\Omega),\|\Delta u\|_2^2=1}}\int_\Omega \frac{e^{32\pi^2(1-\frac{\beta}{4}) u^2(1+\alpha\|u\|_2^2)}}{|x|^\beta}dx. \] These results can be regarded as a further development, in the singular setting, of the theory on the existence of extremals established by Lu and Yang [Adv. Math. (2009)]. Our proof relies on the blow-up analysis of the subcritical maximizers, combined with biharmonic truncation adapted to the singular weight, capacity-type estimates on annular regions and a test function argument. A key novelty of our approach lies in carrying out the blow-up analysis without relying on an explicit expression for the limiting profile near the blow-up point, which is unavailable in the present setting. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first attempt to perform such a blow-up analysis without the explicit form of the limiting profile.

papers.title: Weak-Weak Stability for Multi-Species Nonlocal Cross-Diffusion Systems with Endpoint Lorentz Kernels
papers.abstract: The quantitative weak-weak stability for multi-species nonlocal cross-diffusion systems on the torus is established. The interactions of the species are described by a symmetric, positive semidefinite matrix-valued kernel whose gradient belongs to the endpoint Lorentz space $L^{d,\infty}$, where $d\ge 2$ is the space dimension. The central estimate, formulated in terms of a modulated Hellinger distance-interaction energy, yields uniqueness of solutions with finite Boltzmann entropy and Fisher information. The proof relies on a two-level endpoint mechanism: The Boltzmann entropy controls the interaction energy, while the Fisher information controls the associated force field. Further results are the immediate $L^2$ regularization and the exponential decay to the homogeneous equilibrium. As a particular application, uniqueness and stability for the two-dimensional Poisson-Nernst-Planck system with periodic Coulomb kernels are obtained.

papers.title: Fractional order Orlicz--Sobolev spaces revisited
papers.abstract: The aim of this paper is to revisit our work [J. Funct. Anal. 277 (2019), 333--367], where fractional order Orlicz--Sobolev spaces were introduced and their behavior as the fractional parameter $s\uparrow1$ was studied, and to redo it without assuming the $\Delta_2$ condition on the Young function $G$ or on its complementary function. Since that paper appeared, the theory of these spaces has been considerably developed, and the tools available today allow for a cleaner treatment in full generality. We prove a Bourgain--Brezis--Mironescu type formula as $s\uparrow1$, a compactness and lower semicontinuity result for sequences with bounded energy, a Poincar\'e inequality uniform in $s$, and the $\Gamma$-convergence of the fractional modulars to a local modular on arbitrary open sets. As an application we study the asymptotic behavior of minimizers and of solutions of Dirichlet problems for the fractional $g$-Laplacian as $s\uparrow1$. This version also corrects some errors in the original paper, and it is intended to serve as a more complete and reliable reference for these results.

papers.title: Stability of a Paraboloidal Steady Solution for the 2D Surface Growth Model
papers.abstract: In this paper we consider the stability problem of 2D surface growth model. To be specific, we prove that the small perturbation of the paraboloidal steady solution decays to zero in $L^\infty(\mathbb{R}^2)$. The decay occurs both for the perturbation and its gradient, whose decay rates are $O(t^{-1/2})$ and $O(t^{-1}\log t)$, respectively. The proof is based on the linearization of the perturbation equation and the bootstrap argument to close the statement in nonlinear equation. Sufficient conditions for stability require the initial data and its gradient of the perturbation to be small in $L^1(\mathbb{R}^2)$ and Wiener algebra $\mathcal{A}$. It is notable that the smallness in second derivative is not necessary, which is physically reasonable because large second derivative would lead to high surface energy and it is expected to be relaxed in short time. We also prove existence and uniqueness of mild solution for perturbation equation under those conditions.

papers.title: Weighted Carleson embedding on product of trees in general dimension
papers.abstract: We prove the equivalence of the Carleson embedding on $n$-trees (arbitrary Cartesian product of trees) and the box condition, for arbitrary nonnegative measures and generalized product weights. For product weights, we obtain the sharp coefficient $4^n$. This extends the bi-tree and tri-tree embedding theorems of \cite{AMPVZ} and \cite{MPVZ} to every dimension. We also give two applications of the Carleson embedding: we characterize Carleson measures for the classical Dirichlet space on the polydisc $\mathbb D^n$ and deduce criteria for bounded composition operators from this space into weighted Bergman spaces, generalizing the results from \cite{MPVZ} and \cite{Beslikas2025}. Finally, we define a generalized logarithmic Dirichlet space and characterize its Carleson measures.

papers.title: Local and Global Bifurcation for Axisymmetric Stationary Relativistic Vlasov--Maxwell Equilibria
papers.abstract: We study bifurcation of stationary two-species relativistic Vlasov--Maxwell equilibria on bounded axisymmetric domains. Velocity-moment and elliptic spectral bounds give computable tests for simple crossings, their number and separation, while the local theorem gives a branch-direction formula. Explicit two-species families exhibit electric-only, magnetic-only, and joint field-norm escape.

papers.title: Principal Eigenvalues for Transport-Nonlocal Operators on Compact Manifolds: Ergodic Averages and Quotient Reduction
papers.abstract: We study principal eigenvalues for transport--nonlocal operators on connected compact Riemannian manifolds. Transport changes the natural spectral threshold from the pointwise maximum of the potential to a maximal invariant average. We establish a necessary and sufficient criterion based on a resolvent spectral radius and derive sufficient existence conditions for uniquely ergodic flows and, through quotient reduction, for flows arising from compact abelian Lie group actions. Examples on the two-dimensional torus show that, for weak nonlocal coupling, transport can create or suppress principal eigenvalues, while sphere rotations illustrate how the quotient criterion accommodates singular orbits.

papers.title: Split Hamiltonian structure for Vlasov--Maxwell equations and cylindrical pinch equilibria
papers.abstract: We study the linearized Vlasov--Maxwell equations for cylindrical pinch equilibria, including the classical Bennett pinch, Gaussian equilibria from our earlier work, and a rigidly rotating $\theta$-pinch. Conservation of particle momentum along a symmetry brings the energy principle of Lin and Strauss into these geometries. We work on a graph space for the symmetry component of the vector potential. For the Bennett $z$-pinch the bare potential form has one negative direction, but the particle-number constraint removes it and the entire $z$-independent spectrum lies on the imaginary axis. For a $z$-pinch with variable axial drift, every $z$-independent growing mode is radial. We prove axisymmetric spectral stability for a Gaussian $\theta$-pinch in an explicit range of axis slopes and for a center-peaked, rigidly rotating $\theta$-pinch. In a screw-pinch the helical twist couples the magnetic flux to the particle and electric constraints. The radial equations still separate, and all sufficiently high helical harmonics have imaginary spectrum. For two Gaussian screw-pinch equilibria we verify spectral stability in the full helical symmetry class.

papers.title: Accidental Threefold Dirac Points at the Origin of the Brillouin Zone and Wave-Packet Dynamics
papers.abstract: We study accidental threefold degeneracies at zero quasimomentum for scalar periodic wave operators on the square lattice. At an isolated positive triple eigenvalue, the middle Bloch band has zero linear term. The two outer bands open linearly in every direction precisely when a Gram matrix of coupling coefficients is positive definite. Square symmetry makes the resulting cone isotropic. For weak perturbations of a constant medium, we construct two transverse tuning curves on which a singlet coincides with a doublet away from their common origin. The central band has positive quadratic curvature along each coordinate axis. For a dilute inclusion of size $\eta$, a variational gap condition gives a unique transverse crossing in a contrast interval of order $\eta^{-2}\log(1/\eta)$. The crossing frequency is asymptotic to $\sqrt{2\pi/\log(1/\eta)}$, and the cone speed vanishes linearly with $\eta$, with a coefficient determined by the far-field dipole moment. A three-component Dirac equation approximates positive-frequency wave packets with an error bound explicit in the material coefficients and the spectral separation at zero quasimomentum. When the singlet has nonzero cell mean, the response to a uniform cell source yields effective permittivity and permeability with simple zeros at the crossing frequency. We express their slopes in terms of the singlet mean and the cone speed. The resulting bulk impedance tends to zero in a weak-contrast example and grows inversely with the inclusion size in the dilute high-contrast crystal.

papers.title: Combined quasi-neutral and zero-relaxation limit of Vlasov-Poisson-Fokker-Planck system
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider the combined quasi-neutral and zero-relaxation limit of Vlasov-Poisson-Fokker-Planck system. With well-prepared initial, we show that the convergence from Vlasov-Poisson-Fokker-Planck system for electron and Vlasov-Poisson-Fokker-Planck system for ion to the incompressible Euler equations and compressible Euler equations, respectively.

papers.title: Global large-data strong solutions to the 2D barotropic compressible Navier-Stokes equations with linear bulk viscosity
papers.abstract: This paper concerns the global well-posedness of the two-dimensional(2D) compressible Navier--Stokes equations with density-dependent bulk viscosity and far-field vacuum. We consider the constitutive laws \(P(\rho)=\rho^\gamma\), with \(\gamma>1\), and \(\lambda(\rho)=\rho\), for which the bulk viscosity degenerates in vacuum. Under suitable regularity and weighted integrability assumptions on the initial data, and assuming only that the total mass is positive, we establish the existence and uniqueness of global strong solutions without any restriction on the size of the initial energy or any radial symmetry assumption. The central difficulty is to derive an upper bound for the density on arbitrary finite time intervals in the absence of enhanced bulk dissipation. To overcome this difficulty, we develop a logarithmic energy method based on successive density levels, which exploits the dissipation accumulated along particle trajectories as the density increases. Combined with weighted estimates, pressure estimates, and the analysis of the effective viscous flux and vorticity, this method yields the density bound required to close the global continuation argument. Our result extends the large-data global strong-solution theory for density-dependent viscosity to the critical linear bulk-viscosity law in the general two-dimensional whole-space setting.

papers.title: Persistence and Breakdown of the Initial Gaussian Rate Function for 1D Quasi-Periodic Cubic NLS
papers.abstract: We study rare events for the spatial supremum of the solution amplitude in the 1D cubic nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation with weak nonlinearity and Gaussian quasi-periodic initial data.Under suitable polynomial decay assumptions in Fourier space and a Diophantine condition controlling small divisors arising from spatial quasi-periodicity, we prove that the initial Gaussian rate function persists uniformly on the \emph{critical logarithmic correction time scale} with a \emph{small enough} prefactor. Using the \emph{Akhmediev breather}, we obtain that the same Gaussian rate function \emph{fails} to hold uniformly on this time scale with a \emph{large} prefactor. This also implies that the initial Gaussian rate function cannot, in general, persist uniformly on arbitrarily long polynomial time scales.
